$comment: A9 §3.3 — the witnessed-scheme table. NOT a closed vocabulary: [A9 §3.2] refuses to close `identityScheme`, and this table is the catalogue of the schemes the external corpus actually witnesses, not the list of the schemes that exist. `documentAccountable` is the one bit [A6 §3.2(a)] asks A9 for, and rule I-ACCOUNT ([A9 §3.4]) is the partial function over it that D-ID takes as an input. Grades follow [A6 §2] and [A7 §2]: `primary` = quoted from captured material in this repo, `secondary` = quoted from the source's own analysis.md. Every row's `identifies` is an [SD §1.2] aggregate kind, `party` included since [A8 §9 item 1] minted it at catalog 0.6.4. Before that release `party` was a literal this table carried and the enum did not, and the five `party`-grain rows each named [A8 §9 item 1] as a blocker because their assertions had no `subject`; those blockers are off and `loadIdentitySchemes` now refuses the blocker on ANY row.

witnesses.cite: A-413 §C.2 — numbers serially pre-assigned; a laser-generated BL "is only accountable when a number has been assigned to the form"; lost, stolen and void numbers reported to DoW PPA; audits every 180 days — analysis.md:330-333

witnesses.cite: "The PRO is the document identity, in the URL" — the resource key, not a searchable field; pre-assigned by the shipper from a carrier-issued block or auto-assigned by the carrier if absent; a print form with a check digit — analysis.md:246-255

schemes.note: The one row where `issuerIsTheAuthority` is false for a document-accountable scheme, and the corpus states the mechanism rather than leaving it to be inferred: the carrier owns the numbering and the shipper may draw from a block the carrier issued it, so the assigning party and the vocabulary's owner are routinely different parties. [SD §7.1]'s `issuer` / `vocabularyScope.authority` split is exactly this case, sourced here a second time and outside the `MS2` equipment case it was first argued from.

schemes.authority: the carrier

witnesses.cite: §375.505(b)(16) "Any identification or registration number you assign to the shipment" — captured/cfr-49-375.xml:373; and §375.519(a)(6) offers it as an alternative to the bill of lading number — captured/cfr-49-375.xml:442

schemes.note: ONE witness, and it is primary and captured. [A6 §3.2] already reads §375.505(b)(16) as the model case of a scheme a document merely CARRIES: a required field IN the bill of lading, distinct from the bill of lading's own number, which is why `documentAccountable` is false here and true for `bolCarrier`. This is NOT the van-line registration number — see `vanlineRegistration`, whose authority, scope structure and witness are all different. The rubric's `Covers` column spells both "registration no.".

schemes.authority: the carrier that accepts the bill of lading

witnesses.cite: `shipmentConfirmationNumber`, "Number provided by the carrier to acknowledge they accepted the BOL" (:1308) — a separate acceptance id — analysis.md:310

schemes.note: [A6 §Cross-area] to [A9] calls this "the model case of a scheme over the LODGING rather than over the document", and that is exactly why its bit is `undetermined` rather than false: the subject the corpus names is an ACT — the carrier's acceptance — and [SD §1.2] has no aggregate for an act of accepting. `identifies` is recorded as `document` because the number is carried on the BOL and the BOL is the only subject in the model the sentence can attach to; the honest statement is that the scheme's real subject is not expressible, and A9 records that rather than defaulting the bit. [A1 §Cross-area] to [A9] asked A9 not to collapse the award and the acceptance: this row is where the acceptance survives as its own scheme instead of becoming a second value under `bolCarrier`.

schemes.corpusName: the Government Bill of Lading Office Code (BLOC / GBLOC)
schemes.authority: the Department of Defense personal-property programme

witnesses.cite: "responsibility for a GBLOC can be transferred between offices with an effective date, and TSPs must cross-reference the transfer list for invoicing previous GBLOCs on shipment BLs" — Regionalization p.17; 400NG 2024 Change 5 p.9 — analysis.md, A9-tagged field row
"BLOC — Bill of Lading Office Code; the identity of the OFFICE, and the scope unit for suspensions and blackouts" — analysis.md:335-336

schemes.note: The row that costs the model something already spent. [SD §7.2] sources the identifier's EFFECTIVE INTERVAL twice, and the second of the two is this scheme's mid-life reassignment — so the shared layer leans on a scheme whose subject it cannot express. Nothing here reopens [SD §7.2]: the interval is right and the evidence for it stands. What A9 recorded is that the worked example behind it is one of the FIVE party-grain rows — `scac`, `usDotNumber`, `mcNumber`, `gbloc`, `agentCode`, enumerated by name in `identity-schemes.test.ts`. This note said "six" from publication until catalog 0.6.4, contradicting that gate; [A8 §9 item 1] then took the blocker off and the example is writable. And this row CORROBORATES [A8 §9 item 3]'s branch-grain closure (2026-10-09) without carrying it, which that item's annotation records because its first draft leaned on it: the dtr-part-iv witness glosses the code as the identity of the OFFICE, but the dp3-400ng witness on this same row has responsibility for a GBLOC transferring between offices with an effective date — which is what [SD §7.2] sources the effective interval from, and what stops this row identifying an office the way `scac` identifies a carrier. `agentCode` carries the closure.

schemes.authority: the van line

witnesses.cite: a 7-digit hierarchical agent id whose trailing three digits are the branch, plus `SvcProvDataRecipient` naming the receiving branch per push (SOE p.2) — analysis.md:363, and quoted in [A8 §9 item 1]
`parentAgentCode` and `/Agents/{agentCode}/Family` — column names only, per [A8 §9 item 1] — analysis.md

schemes.note: The one party-grain scheme whose structure the corpus publishes: the code CARRIES the branch, so the identifier encodes a hierarchy the model would otherwise have to store. Recorded for A8, which owed both the party entity and the branch grain, and ACTED ON by neither round that closed them: [A8 §9 item 1] minted the party at catalog 0.6.4 and [A8 §9 item 3] closed the branch grain on 2026-10-09 by reading THIS row rather than by adding anything — `gbloc` corroborates, with the caveat its own row states. A branch is a party because the identifier that identifies it identifies a party — 7 digits, the trailing three being the branch. What is still owed is the HIERARCHY the code encodes: `parentAgentCode` is a party-to-party relation no `AssertionType` holds, and the gate is `identity-schemes.test.ts`'s item-3 block.

witnesses.cite: A-406 §A.11 p.5 / A-402 §D.5.a(2) p.17 — 9 digits, YY + Julian day of entry + a 4-digit sequence within that day; a split shipment gets its own control number per increment — analysis.md:337-338, and [SD §7.4]
"SIT control number" among the identifier families — analysis.md:448

schemes.note: Already spent: [SD §7.4] uses this scheme to answer `fork-order`'s foreclosure #3 — the stay grain does not need an identifier of our own because the industry publishes one. [A5 §Cross-area] to [A9] says so and hands it on. A9 adds only that it is one of the three CONSTRUCTED schemes in the table (with `tcn` and `vanlineRegistration`'s triple), where the value's own positions carry meaning — and that [SD §7.5]'s canonicalise-to-match policy is safe over a constructed value precisely because it is forbidden from mutating `value`.

schemes.authority: the Department of Defense

witnesses.cite: 17 positions, with position 15 typed by shipment kind (B = UB DPM, J = UB TGBL, H = HHG DPM, K = HHG TGBL, P = POV) — A-402 §F.10.a(15) p.32 — analysis.md:339-340

schemes.note: A constructed scheme whose position 15 classifies the shipment. Worth one sentence to A2 and no more: the classification is IN the identifier, so a consumer that parses it is deriving a shipment type from a value [SD §7.5] forbids canonicalising and [A2 §3.3] refuses to publish a vocabulary for. A9 reads the position as evidence about the scheme, never as a fact about the shipment.

"inventory item numbers" among the identifier families — analysis.md:344-345

`MS2`, "the owner, the identification number ASSIGNED BY THAT OWNER, and the type of equipment" — analysis.md:361-363

schemes.authority: the van line — and the corpus witnesses TWO of its systems issuing under separate schemes

witnesses.cite: `QPDTripNumber` (10 digits) and `CamisTripNumber` (5 digits), both carried on every trip-bearing event (SOE p.2) — one trip, two schemes, both authoritative — analysis.md:374 and [SD §7.4]

schemes.note: Already spent by [SD §7.4] as the worked case for arity N per I-KEY. Carried as ONE row rather than two because what the corpus publishes is two number FORMATS from one authority with no statement of which vocabulary is which — `definedNotMerelyNamed` is false for that reason. Splitting it into two schemes here would be an authored decision dressed as a reading.

schemes.authority: the packing agent that applies the seal

witnesses.cite: applied at the residence for international/Code 2 containers, with "seal numbers annotated on the inventory cross-referencing the container number" — HHG §C.11.i pp.43-44 — the A9-tagged field row

`M7` Seal Numbers, a segment at position 160 of loop 0150 beside `MS2` — captured/stedi-212-215-structure-notes.md:72. The capture proves the segment exists in the structure and carries no definition.

schemes.note: Two witnesses from unrelated regimes, and the DP3 one publishes a CROSS-REFERENCE obligation rather than a scheme: the seal number is annotated against the container number. That is [A9 §3.5]'s subject — a correlation the corpus states as an obligation on a document, which the model expresses as two identity assertions and no link.
